sources.title: P-adic valuation
sources.enterprise_use: Records the established p-adic valuation laws v_p(xy)=v_p(x)+v_p(y) and v_p(x+y)>=min(v_p(x),v_p(y)), with equality when the two input valuations differ. R004 specializes these standard facts into future-safe quotient/carry and translation-trie pressure tests.
sources.not_claimed: P-adic valuations, non-Archimedean norms, and their ultrametric laws are established mathematics and are not Enterprise Math inventions.

sources.title: First steps in tropical geometry
sources.enterprise_use: Provides a direct prior-art boundary for min-plus/tropical algebra. R004's valuation-off-diagonal min rule must not be advertised as invention of a new min-plus arithmetic.
sources.not_claimed: Tropical semirings, tropicalization, min-plus algebra and tropical geometry are established prior mathematics.

sources.title: Sylvester's identity and multistep integer-preserving Gaussian elimination
sources.enterprise_use: Provides the established fraction-free exact-linear-algebra precedent for future Enterprise Math integer constraint solvers. R004 does not implement or claim the Bareiss algorithm here.
sources.not_claimed: Fraction-free Gaussian elimination and integer-preserving elimination are established symbolic-computation methods.

sources.title: Integer-Valued Polynomials: From Combinatorics to Number Theory, p-adic Analysis, Commutative and Non-Commutative Algebra
sources.enterprise_use: Provides the modern prior-art boundary for integer-valued-polynomial and binomial-coordinate methods. R004 uses only elementary binomial count identities and does not claim that integer-valued or binomial-basis polynomial calculus is new.
sources.not_claimed: Integer-valued polynomials, generalized factorial/orderings, p-adic analysis and binomial-coordinate methods are established prior mathematics.

sources.title: Mathlib.GroupTheory.FiniteAbelian.Basic
sources.enterprise_use: Official Mathlib documentation records the established structure theorem that finite abelian groups decompose as direct sums of prime-power cyclic ZMod components. R004 uses this only as prior-art support for its quotient exponent-profile interpretation.
sources.not_claimed: The structure theorem for finite abelian groups and prime-power cyclic decomposition are established mathematics, not Enterprise Math results.

sources.title: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.PID
sources.enterprise_use: Official Mathlib documentation provides Smith-normal-form bases for finite-rank submodules over principal ideal domains, supplying the prior-art boundary for diagonal invariant-factor descriptions of quotient relation modules.
sources.not_claimed: Smith normal form, invariant factors over PIDs, and diagonalization of submodule inclusions are established mathematics.

sources.title: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.Finite.Quotient
sources.enterprise_use: Official Mathlib documentation expresses finite free-module quotients over PIDs as products of cyclic quotients using Smith coefficients. R004 uses this as a prior-art boundary for converting an additive future congruence into a structured quotient-module view.
sources.not_claimed: Finite free-module quotient decomposition by Smith coefficients is established algebra and formalized prior work.
